title: Model anchoring semantics for API/SDK: tags, semver ranges, and commit hashes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a single, predictable anchoring model for user-specified model references in the Redwood API and SDKs. Users can currently pin models by tag (e.g., 'stable'), semver (e.g., 'v1.2.x'), and commit-like opaque hashes (e.g., 'sha256:abcd...'). This ticket clarifies the resolution precedence, matching rules (exact vs prefix vs range), fallback semantics, and how performance profiles are published and bound to the resolved model version. The goal is to make resolution deterministic, observable, and safe for production rollouts while preserving ergonomics for users who want flexible tags.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Resolution precedence is documented and implemented: exact commit/hash > exact semver tag > semver range > named tag (most recent matching) > fallback policy.
2) SDK validates incoming model reference syntax and returns clear error codes for ambiguous or invalid pins.
3) Server publishes which concrete model-version (id/hash) satisfied the request and the performance profile id used, returned in response metadata and visible in Console traces.

4) A lightweight compatibility check runs during onboarding: if a requested semver or tag resolves to a model with no performance profile, the system triggers an automated profiling job or returns a documented warning with a non-blocking flag.
5) Fallback policies (none, auto-fallback-to-compatible, route-to-lower-tier) are configurable and honored by the resolver; tests cover each mode.
6) Migration path documented for existing customers using floating tags; deprecation warnings emitted for tags that would become ambiguous under new rules.
background: We support multiple user-facing ways to refer to models. Historically, resolution rules were underspecified and varied across SDKs, which led to surprising rollouts: e.g., a 'stable' tag moved to a new major that broke latency guarantees, and customers observed different resolved ids between the REST API and Python SDK. We also need a clear contract for when and how performance profiles are associated with a logical reference so customers can reason about latency/cost tradeoffs.
decision_record: Adopt a deterministic resolver with strict precedence: commit/hash (exact) wins, then semver exact, then semver range (highest matching semver by semver ordering), then named tag (most recent model published to tag). Fallback policies are explicit; default is 'no fallback' for hosted API and 'auto-fallback-to-compatible' for Dedicated customers with policy opt-in. Performance profiles are immutable artifacts bound to a specific model-version id and published alongside the model onboarding. SDKs and the API return 'resolved_model_id' and 'performance_profile_id' in response headers/body metadata.
tradeoffs: Stricter semantics reduce surprise but increase friction for users who rely on floating tags; we mitigate with tooling (preview resolves, dry-run) and deprecation warnings.
Automatically profiling models on first resolution increases infra cost and onboarding latency; we make it opt-out/priority-queued for non-critical tiers.
Tight coupling of profiles to model id improves reproducibility but requires storage/retention policies; we'll add TTLs and archival for old profiles.
implementation_notes: API: Add query param / header 'resolve_preview=true' to return the would-be resolved id without executing the model; implement deterministic resolver function in route handler.
SDK: Add a ModelRef object that parses inputs and exposes kind (commit|semver_exact|semver_range|tag) and a validate() method that returns user-friendly errors.
Resolver: Implement a single service in runtime that takes ModelRef and customer context and returns {resolved_id, resolution_path, profile_id}. Persist resolution_path for auditing.
Performance profiles: extend onboarding pipeline to accept a 'profile_ready' flag. If missing, enqueue profiling job and return a 'profile_pending' status in metadata.
Backward compatibility: add a feature-flagged compatibility layer for 8 weeks to allow existing SDK users to opt into old behavior.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge resolver and SDK parsing changes behind feature flag; publish docs and deprecation warnings for ambiguous tags.
Week 1-2: Enable feature flag for internal and beta customers; collect differences between old and new resolution using telemetry.
Week 3: Opt-in Dedicated customers can select 'auto-fallback' policy; hosted remains 'no fallback' by default.
Week 4: Default-on rollout once no high-risk diffs observed; provide 30-day soft deprecation window for customers with ambiguous tags.
Post-rollout: Monitor support volumes and run a migration assistance program for customers with breakages.
test_plan: Unit tests for ModelRef parsing and validation (invalid semver strings, ambiguous tags).
Integration tests for resolver precedence with mocked model catalog entries covering edge cases (overlapping semver ranges, tag reassignment).
E2E tests: API + SDK roundtrip asserting 'resolved_model_id' and 'performance_profile_id' present in response metadata.
Chaos test: simulate delayed profiling jobs and assert response behavior under 'profile_pending'.
Performance test: ensure resolution adds <1ms median latency for typical queries and <5ms p95.
monitoring: Telemetry: emit 'resolution_change' events when a logical reference resolves to a different model id than previous week.
Alerting: high-rate 'profile_pending' for a customer triggers onboarding ops ticket (P0 if >5% of requests impacted for 24h).
Dashboards: per-customer and per-tag breakdowns showing resolved ids, profile coverage, and latency deltas caused by model swaps.
